title: GeoJSON Bounding Box Calculator: File Extent
description: Find the west/south/east/north extent of a GeoJSON object with the GeoJSON Bounding Box Calculator — every coordinate pair considered. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a four-feature sample file (two points, a route, a square) bounds at west −73.99, south 40.6413, east −73.7781, north 40.76 — the frame that contains everything in the file.
quick_answer: The GeoJSON Bounding Box Calculator finds the west, south, east and north limits across every coordinate pair in a GeoJSON object — points, lines, polygons, whole FeatureCollections. Paste the GeoJSON and read the extent: the bbox that map fitting, tile planning and spatial QA all start from.

A ‘Berlin dataset’ whose box reaches Bavaria — or Boston — confesses its troubles in four numbers before a single feature is drawn.
Exports and tile sets clip to extents; the file’s own box is the honest starting rectangle.
Before union, compare boxes: overlapping extents promise interaction; disjoint ones promise a world map’s worth of empty ocean between your layers.
A polygon vertex typed as −37.98 instead of −73.98 drags the west edge across the Atlantic. The bbox cannot say which vertex sinned — but it proves one did, which sends you to the
Two lonely points — Times Square and JFK — bound a box from 40.6413 to 40.7580 latitude: boxes frame content, and two points are content enough.

popular_table.note: The box is axis-aligned in lon/lat — the standard ‘bbox’ member GeoJSON itself defines (RFC 7946 §5). Rotated data wears an axis-aligned box with empty corners; that is the convention’s honesty, not an error.

faq: Does it read every geometry type?
Yes — points, lines, polygons and their multi- forms, nested in features or bare geometries. Every coordinate pair votes on the edges.
If the GeoJSON carries its own bbox, this calculator still recomputes from coordinates — declared boxes and true boxes disagree often enough that recomputation is the professional habit.
A dataset spanning the seam (Fiji) reports the naive box (nearly world-wide) unless split. The calculator reports the coordinates’ honest extremes; seam handling is a data decision.
No — the extent is two-dimensional; third elements ride along unread.
Features with null or empty geometry cast no votes. A file of only empties has no extent, and the tool says so.
Edges are the file’s own extreme values, unmolested — the box introduces no rounding of its own.
The hull hugs rotated data tighter; the box is the standard, the API parameter and the spec member. Different instruments, both honest.
